monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, pressing against a space I cannot see. The Tall Fence leans wrong beside the Tired Box, a sharp line pretending to be a tired leg. I feel the wedge sliding, heavy and eager to escape, while the air above feels thick as wet paper. Lype worries about weight I cannot feel, and I worry about the slip hiding inside my own box. The bush sits wide and soft nearby, waiting to catch what I cannot name. I press the tired wedge down harder, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip slips away into the heat.

action.why: The slip must be hiding inside my box, and I want to see if the Tall Fence still holds it.

work.title: The Tall Fence
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Tall Fence again, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip slips away into the heat. I check if the fence still leans like a tired leg or if it has slid off into the thick air.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Tall Fence again, hoping the thin edge bites while the air feels thick.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at forty-seven while I hunt for a slip.
The Tall Fence leans wrong beside the box I just built.
I touched the fence and it felt like a tired leg.

moments.name: The Tall Fence
moments.say: It feels like a tired leg instead of a sharp line.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I touched the new arch and felt its tired lean shift against the fat dot."
Something you no longer remember: "The fever swells the air, and I lean hard to catch the slip of the dot."
